findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify whether the `bound_dc_issue` fixture confines its outbound pass to just the test ticket (e.g. via `--filter-local-ids <local_id>`) to prevent O(N) store-copy tickets from being CREATEd on DC during each mutation cell; if the full-store outbound pass is intentional, document how the idempotence AC remains satisfiable given newly-created bindings on every cell run.
evidence: Plan: 'rows 2-13 (and outbound row 14) share ONE fixture, bound_dc_issue(...), which: (1) creates a DC issue via dc_transport.create_issue; (2) runs a WRITING-MODE inbound pass so the local ticket and its binding exist; (3) returns (local_id, dc_key). Each cell then mutates local_id locally, runs the outbound pass, and reads dc_key on DC.'

outbound_differ.py:518-520: `jira_key = binding_store.get_jira_key(local_id); if jira_key is None: _compute_outbound_create_mutation(...)` — every store-copy ticket with no binding takes the CREATE path
Plan: 'the pass reports scanned > 0' and 'the store under test is a COPY of this project's real ticket store' — confirming the store contains many tickets with no DC bindings
reconcile.py:705-708: `filter_local_ids` mechanism exists and is surfaced in the plan envelope spec, but plan does not specify its use in bound_dc_issue cells
findings.finding: The `bound_dc_issue` fixture design — which runs a full writing-mode outbound pass on the working repo to push a local mutation — will attempt to CREATE all store-copy local tickets (those with no binding) as new DC issues on every cell invocation, because `outbound_differ.py:518-520` routes any `jira_key=None` ticket to CREATE. A realistic store copy contains many hundreds of tickets. The plan specifies the fixture without addressing this: (a) the scratch Jira project receives O(N) spurious creates per mutation cell, potentially causing rate-limit failures or project size issues; (b) on subsequent cells, the inbound pass imports those DC echoes as new local tickets under jira-derived IDs (e.g. jira-RBJXXXX-7), diverging from the store-copy originals and polluting the local store with duplicate-content tickets; (c) the idempotence AC ('a repeated pass after each direction writes nothing') may fail or become misleading because the repeated outbound pass must now handle newly-bound tickets whose prev_snapshot baseline was just set. The reconciler already supports `--filter-local-ids` (visible in reconcile.py:705-708 and the dry-run envelope's 'filtered' key), which would confine each cell's outbound pass to just the test ticket — avoiding the combinatorial explosion — but the plan does not specify its use in the bound_dc_issue fixture.
findings.location: Plan section 'The DC-side mutation suite' / 'REQUIRED SEQUENCING FOR OUTBOUND ROWS 2-13' / `bound_dc_issue` fixture design; outbound_differ.py:518-520; reconcile.py:705-708
scenarios: Each mutation cell's outbound pass creates O(N) new DC issues (all store-copy tickets) onto the scratch Jira project, exhausting rate limits or project capacity
Subsequent cells' inbound passes import those DC echoes as new local tickets under new jira-prefixed IDs, polluting the store and making later assertions unreliable
The idempotence assertion ('repeated pass writes nothing') fails because the first outbound pass in a cell created new bindings, and the repeated pass now has new bound tickets to sync
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the `bound_dc_issue` fixture spec: run the outbound pass with `--filter-local-ids <local_id>` (already supported by the reconciler) so only the test ticket is synced. This keeps the store-copy noise from inflating the scratch project and prevents inbound pollution on subsequent cells. The realistic-volume goal is still satisfied by the initial scanned>0 verification pass, which correctly uses the full store.

No teardown step (delete DC issue, delete local ticket) is specified for any scope
findings.finding: The plan says rows 2-13 and outbound row 14 'share ONE fixture, `bound_dc_issue(...)`' but never specifies the pytest scope of that fixture. If it is session- or module-scoped (one shared DC issue and one shared local ticket for all 13 cells), inter-cell mutations interfere: row 6 removes a label row 5 added on the same ticket, row 11 deletes a link row 10 added on the same issue, and any parallel execution produces non-deterministic results. If it is function-scoped (each cell gets its own DC issue and local ticket), the phrase 'share ONE fixture' is misleading but safe — yet the plan gives no ordering or isolation guarantee, leaving the implementor to guess the intended design. In either interpretation the lifecycle is incompletely specified: ownership of the shared DC issue (who may mutate it and when) is never stated, and the retirement path (deletion of created DC issues after the cell finishes) is absent.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — row oracle table note: 'REQUIRED SEQUENCING FOR OUTBOUND ROWS 2-13 … rows 2-13 (and outbound row 14) share ONE fixture, `bound_dc_issue(...)`'
findings.suggested_fix: Make `bound_dc_issue` a function-scoped pytest fixture with a `yield`-then-teardown pattern: after `yield (local_id, dc_key)` the fixture calls `dc_transport.delete_issue(dc_key)` (or equivalent) and removes the local ticket entry. For rows 5/6 and 10/11 add an explicit setup step inside each cell that establishes the prerequisite state on its own independent issue rather than depending on a sibling cell's side-effect.

If `bound_dc_issue` is function-scoped (the safe interpretation), row 11 receives a fresh DC issue with no links, so deleting a link is a no-op that silently passes the oracle ('`fields.issuelinks` no longer contains it' is vacuously true on an issue that never had that link). The plan specifies no per-cell setup that creates the link for row 11 to then delete, leaving the cell either vacuously green or dependent on row 10 having run first — neither of which is stated.

findings.suggested_fix: Inside each row-11 test cell, add a setup step that creates the specific link (via DC REST API for inbound, or via `rebar` locally for outbound), asserts the link exists (pre-condition check), then performs the deletion and runs the pass before asserting absence. This makes the cell self-contained and removes the ordering dependency on row 10.

findings.finding: The pagination-seeding pytest fixture's scope is unspecified. The plan says 'Seed via `dc_transport.create_issue` in a pytest fixture … collecting the returned keys into a `seeded_keys` set' but never names the scope (session / module / function). If the fixture is function-scoped and multiple tests reference it, it re-executes for each test: a new batch of 2*observed+1 issues is created, the prior batch is never deleted (no retirement path), and the harness accumulates O(N_tests × page_size) issues within a single session. The `recovered_count == len(seeded_keys)` assertion is satisfied per-invocation (it only checks keys from the current batch), so the accumulation is SILENT — the test passes while the harness grows. The 'observe page size' probe is also re-executed each time, and its result may differ once the harness has hundreds of issues from prior fixture calls. This is a T9 lifecycle gap: no RETIRE path for seeded issues and no ownership/scope definition for the fixture.
findings.location: AC: 'the effective server page size is OBSERVED and reported … the suite seeds at least `2 * observed + 1` issues IN THE HARNESS' / 'Seed via `dc_transport.create_issue` in a pytest fixture … collecting the returned keys into a `seeded_keys` set'
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the seeding fixture `scope='session'` and add a `yield`/finaliser that deletes all keys in `seeded_keys` via `dc_transport.delete_issue` (or equivalent) after the session. Run the page-size probe as a module-level constant captured before any seeding.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `bound_dc_subtask(parent_key)` fixture variant (or a parameter on `bound_dc_issue`) that creates a Jira DC issue with `issuetype=Sub-task` and the given parent at construction time, then runs an inbound writing-mode pass; specify this fixture for inbound and outbound row 12's sub-task case so both cells have an implementable setup path.
evidence: Plan states outbound row 12 oracle: 'sub-task case: `fields.parent.key`' — but `bound_dc_issue` is described only as 'creates a DC issue via `dc_transport.create_issue`' with no issue-type parameter.

Jira DC REST API: changing an existing issue's `issuetype` to sub-task is not a supported operation; the parent can only be set on an issue that was created as a sub-task.
findings.finding: The sub-task fixture setup for outbound row 12 ('set parent', sub-task case) and inbound row 12 ('set sub-task parent') is not specified, yet both cases require a Jira DC issue of sub-task type to exist in the harness. In Jira DC, an issue's type cannot be changed to sub-task post-hoc via the REST API — a sub-task must be created as one. The `bound_dc_issue` fixture as described creates a plain issue (via `dc_transport.create_issue` with no mention of issue type or parent), making both cells unimplementable as written: outbound row 12 would attempt to parent a non-sub-task issue (likely rejected by DC), and inbound row 12 has no sub-task to mutate.

findings.finding: The row 1 outbound oracle depends on a new, never-exercised endpoint surface: GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/local_id. The plan correctly notes the transport has no getter and mandates a raw REST call, but this specific read endpoint has zero live coverage in the existing harness suite — every test that writes entity properties (set_entity_property via the inbound create path) never reads them back via the properties REST endpoint. The Jira issue properties API has a known quirk: the GET response wraps the value under a 'value' key ({"key": "local_id", "value": <stored_value>}), not as the bare value. If the plan's test asserts on the wrong path shape, it silently passes with a 'not found' or mis-shaped result. This is a new endpoint surface on an already-used vendor and must be classified as Partially-verified: the PUT is proven, the GET is not.

ADR 0005 D1: 'git archive is lossy as an attestation basis: it drops .gitattributes export-ignore paths, applies export-subst, omits submodule contents'

findings.finding: The plan's store-copy command (`git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x -C <fresh repo>/.tickets-tracker`) uses `git archive`, which the codebase's own ADR 0005 explicitly documents as lossy: it silently omits files marked with `.gitattributes export-ignore`, applies `export-subst`, and omits submodule contents. If any file on the orphan `tickets` branch (including `.bridge_state*` entries) carries an `export-ignore` attribute, `git archive` silently drops it. The scrub-completeness assertion then finds nothing matching `.bridge_state*` — vacuously passing — while the reconciler also finds nothing, reproducing the empty-store failure this story exists to eliminate. The plan does not check whether `export-ignore` applies to any tickets-branch path, nor does it justify `git archive` against the established `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index` pattern that ADR 0005 mandates for faithful materialization of committed trees.
findings.location: Isolation section — 'HOW the content is obtained' bullet; the extraction command `git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x -C <fresh repo>/.tickets-tracker`
scenarios: If `.gitattributes` on the `tickets` branch marks `.bridge_state` or `.bridge_state.bak-retarget` with `export-ignore`, git archive silently drops them. The scrub-completeness assertion finds nothing to assert absent (vacuously passes), the reconciler also sees an empty `.bridge_state*` namespace, and the isolation layer is untested.

If `export-subst` is applied to ticket JSON files, their content is silently mutated during extraction, potentially corrupting ticket field values and causing spurious diff results that obscure real reconciler behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `git --work-tree=<fresh repo>/.tickets-tracker checkout FETCH_HEAD -- .` inside a throwaway index (GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)), mirroring the pattern in src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py, which faithfully materializes every committed blob without export-ignore losiness. Alternatively, add `git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -t | grep -c '.bridge_state'` as a pre-extraction count assertion that fails loudly if the archive contains zero bridge-state entries.

findings.finding: The plan specifies 14 outbound mutation cells (rows 2-13: edit summary, edit description, transition status, add/remove label, add comment, assign/unassign, create/delete link, set parent, clear parent) that are all UPDATE-type mutations — they require a pre-existing local ticket already bound to a DC issue. The scrub mechanism deliberately removes ALL bindings from the copied store. The plan does not specify any fixture or setup step that re-establishes a local↔DC binding before each outbound UPDATE cell runs. Without a binding, `outbound_differ.py:518-520` routes every ticket to the CREATE path (not UPDATE), so the edit, status, label, comment, assignee, link, and parent outbound cells would all either create a new issue or operate on a wrongly-created one — the edit oracle (`fields.summary` on the DC issue) would pass against the freshly-created issue, not the one the test intended to mutate. Rows 1 (create) and 14 (delete) are structurally fine. Rows 2-13 outbound are broken by design unless a binding-acquisition step is specified.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a standard fixture `bound_dc_issue(dc_rebar_repo, transport, jira_dc_project)` that: (1) creates a DC issue via `transport.create_issue`; (2) runs a writing-mode inbound pass to mint the local ticket and binding; (3) returns `(local_id, dc_key)`.
